summary: The bill directs NOAA to research how the public receives, interprets, and responds to hurricane forecasts and warnings by reviewing existing knowledge, filling data gaps through social and economic studies, assessing vulnerable populations, and running a pilot survey on preparedness in hurricane-prone areas.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the NOAA Administrator to carry out new research and development activities (including data collection, pilot studies, assessments, and cost-benefit analyses) on public response to hurricane forecasts. This requires federal resources and therefore expands government spending, though the scope is limited to a targeted NOAA program rather than broad appropriations.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare delivery, insurance, or public/private coverage models.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration pathways, enforcement, or border policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.

While the research involves NOAA (an environmental agency) and hurricane forecasting, the bill focuses exclusively on social, behavioral, and economic studies of public response rather than environmental protections, regulations, or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement spending.
